title: Cycle capacity lattice: prioritized staffing, buffer lanes, and guided scope trims
creator: Aisha Khatri
body:
Background:
We repeatedly hit mid-cycle firefights where teams scramble to reallocate engineers, cut scope, or postpone initiatives without a consistent rubric. Existing playbooks are fragmented across documents (trim recommendations, staffing request forms, and surge handoff notes).

Objective:
Create a single operational playbook — the "Cycle Capacity Lattice" — that combines (1) a prioritized staffing policy, (2) distinct buffer lanes for emergency capacity, and (3) a guided scope-trim rubric tied to OKR value and risk. The playbook should make mid-cycle decisions auditable, predictable, and fast.

Scope (what this ticket delivers):
- A documented decision flow chart for mid-cycle capacity rebalancing.
- Scoring rubric for scope trim candidates (OKR alignment, user impact, technical risk, unblock potential).
- Definition and sizing guidance for three buffer lanes: Tactical (24–72h), Short-term surge (1–3 weeks), Strategic reserve (cycle-end buffer).
- Template staffing request form and approval matrix (who can reassign, who must approve).
- Runbook for triage: morning signal checks, cross-functional sync cadence, and escalation paths.
- A simulation worksheet (CSV template) to model tradeoffs between staffing moves and launch dates.

Key decisions and tradeoffs discussed so far:
- Conservative buffer vs. aggressive staffing: we recommend a 6–10% tactical buffer per org and a separate 8% short-term surge pool to avoid constant re-triage. This favors predictability at the cost of some underutilization.
- Scoring weights: OKR alignment (40%), user-facing regressions (25%), engineering effort (15%), unblock multiplier (10%), compliance/regulatory risk (10%). Open question: whether to double-weight customer-reported regressions; flagged for leadership review.
- Approval tiers: Team leads can approve tactical lane moves; product council sign-off required for reassigning >2 FTE across initiatives or when strategic reserve is touched. This keeps velocity while protecting high-visibility bets.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Playbook doc checked into Confluence with 'accepted' header and an examples appendix.
2) 3 teams run the simulation worksheet on an in-flight cycle and report results (template filled) in the cycle retro.
3) Approval matrix and staffing request form available as an OAA (one-click) template in Notion/Drive.
4) Runbook steps automated into the weekly cadence (owner assigned for morning signal).

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (review): Share draft with PM, Eng, Design leads; gather feedback.
- Week 2 (pilot): Apply to two mid-sized teams for an upcoming cycle tranche and collect metrics (time-to-decision, number of rescoped tickets, perceived fairness).
- Week 3 (iterate): Revise scoring weights and buffer sizes based on pilot data.
- Week 4 (launch): Publish playbook and add to 'Cycle Operations' section of onboarding.

Metrics to track post-launch:
- Median time to scope-trim decision (goal < 72 hours).
- Number of cross-team reassignments per cycle (expected < 3 major reassigns).
- Percentage of initiatives moved to strategic reserve.
- Qualitative fairness score from affected teams (survey).

Open items / blockers:
- Need legal input on any constraints when reassigning engineers attached to enterprise customer work (ticketed to ENG-1842).
- Need direct access to cycle-level utilization dashboards (dashboard request submitted: internal ticket DT-331).
- Final sign-off from Head of Product and Head of Eng on approval matrix (meeting requested 2026-03-14).

Recommended next steps (owner assignment):
- Draft final Confluence doc: Aisha (owner) by 2026-03-10.
- Pilot coordination: Liam (assignee) to run pilot with Team Atlas and Team Harbor by 2026-03-19.
- Simulation data collection: Data analyst (ad-hoc, request sent to analytics@redwood.ai).

Links to artifacts and examples:
- Prior scope-trim examples (retro notes): https://drive.google.com/example-retro
- Existing staffing request form (prototype): https://docs.google.com/forms/example-staffing

If approved, this playbook will reduce ad-hoc triage, speed decisions, and create a transparent record for mid-cycle tradeoffs — supporting our mission to keep inference feature launches predictable and aligned to business value.
